tasks.how: Read the brief and fill the START HERE tab once: subject (brand, product or topic), markets, languages, period N and N-1 (exact start and end dates), client questions, client deadline and internal deadlines (end of production, peer review, feedback day). Log every scope decision (what is in, what is out) in the scope log.
tasks.check: Period dates, markets and deadlines are written once in START HERE and reused everywhere else.

tasks.how: Create the project folder on the Drive with the agreed naming convention. Copy the latest master versions of the production file (this file) and of the deck template. Never start from a previous client's digest.
tasks.check: Files come from the current master versions and follow the naming convention.
tasks.output: Project folder with production file and deck

tasks.how: Allocate analyst and reviewer time in Float. Book the peer review slot and the feedback day in calendars before production starts.
tasks.check: Review slot booked before production starts.

tasks.how: Look for a previous edition on the same brand or category: Radarly query, R&R facets, product mapping, topic keyword sets, launch calendar, brand assets. Reuse what is still valid and list what must be updated. Reuse across clients only with explicit internal approval.
tasks.tools: Drive, queries library, building-radarly-queries and building-corpus-facets skills
tasks.check: Reused assets listed with their date; outdated elements flagged.

tasks.how: Review the official website, Instagram and TikTok accounts and recent press. Note the brand story, ambassadors, launches, campaigns and events of the period. Log each one with its date and link in the launch calendar (used in the 'Monthly evolution & peaks' step to explain monthly peaks). Save the top links. Start writing the story: what type of content you see and what the brand pushes.
tasks.check: Launch and campaign dates of the period are noted with sources.
tasks.output: Context notes, launch calendar, top links

tasks.how: List official products from the website (name, line, variants, launch date) and map each to its names in the corpus. Flag products absent from the corpus. New launches absent from the reviews corpus must be reported to the lead: they bias the reviews results.
tasks.check: Every official product is mapped or flagged as absent.

tasks.how: Check volumes of the brand and of each candidate competitor per market in Live Fix to confirm feasibility. Flag low bases to the lead before the competitor set is frozen.
tasks.check: Volumes large enough per market and competitor; low bases flagged to the lead.

tasks.how: Agree the final competitor set with the lead (and with the client if the brief requires it) based on the pre-check. Write it in START HERE.
tasks.check: Competitor set frozen before the query and R&R extraction.

tasks.how: Start from the library query if one exists (see the Reuse check step). Include brand + product names (from the product mapping) + brand-specific hashtags, in the languages of the markets. Exclude out-of-scope universes (e.g. fashion when the scope is beauty).
tasks.check: Boolean syntax: uppercase AND / OR / NOT, closed quotes and parentheses.

tasks.how: Read a random sample of posts spread across platforms and markets in Radarly before launching the query. Identify noise vectors (homonyms, out-of-scope universes, giveaways, resellers), add exclusions, iterate until precision is acceptable. Get the lead's validation.
tasks.check: Precision checked on a sample; noise vectors and exclusions documented.

tasks.how: Save the validated query in the queries library with its metadata: brand, client, markets, languages, date, precision estimate, exclusions and the reason for each. Queries are internal IP: never share them with the client.
tasks.check: Library entry dated and linked to the project.

tasks.how: Create the Radarly project: markets, languages, platforms (Instagram, TikTok, X, Reddit, Blogs, Forums, YouTube), 24 months covering N and N-1.
tasks.check: Same settings for N and N-1. X is named X (not Twitter).

tasks.how: If Radarly returns only one month of YouTube, take YouTube from Synthesio / Meltwater, or extrapolate the available month(s) to 12 months. Write the method in the Notes column of tab 5-A.
tasks.check: Method written in the Notes column of tab 5-A.

tasks.how: Create a Trajaan project per market with the keyword set: brand + category, product names, variants (e.g. '[brand] edp', '[product] by [brand]'), local-language forms.
tasks.check: Same keyword set for every market (translated where needed).

tasks.how: Use the latest Semantiweb Ratings & Reviews Deduplicate corpus. Apply the Solr period filters from START HERE to brand, competitors and category, using the facet library. Request the category benchmark (attributes + average rating, all markets in scope) from its owner on day 1.
tasks.tools: Corpus Manager / Live Fix, building-corpus-facets skill
tasks.check: Identical filters for brand, competitors and category.

tasks.how: Export the standard Radarly views for N and N-1: volume by platform, sentiment by platform, monthly volume, volume by market (incl. undetermined), top words, emojis, associated brands. Save the raw exports in the project folder.
tasks.check: Same date range and filters on every export; files named by view and period.

tasks.how: Change colours to the brand DNA, logos (latest versions from the websites: client + Semantiweb + brand, right universe), header, visuals (HQ, not distorted), dates, footnotes and flags. Keep the 'Social insight snack' band and scope box in black.
tasks.check: Checklist tab 9, 'General' and 'Page 1' sections.

tasks.how: Enter N and N-1 volumes per platform with source and method. Add the TikTok estimate manually and document its logic. Report Reddit (US) and Blogs & Forums (other markets) as one merged line.
tasks.check: All platforms sum to 100%. Every estimate or extrapolation has a note. Trend column reviewed.

tasks.how: Enter positive / neutral / negative counts per platform. For TikTok, use the coded TikTok sample and label it Estimated.
tasks.check: Sentiment base coverage vs volume base checked (line under the table).

tasks.how: Enter monthly volumes (Radarly month by month + brand reviews month by month). Explain every flagged peak with its driver (launch, campaign, ambassador, event, viral video) and a supporting link from the launch calendar (Brand / product / topic check).
tasks.check: Months in English. No peak left unexplained.

tasks.how: Enter identified volumes per market and the undetermined volume. Rank markets for the deck flags (ranking only, no % or volumes on the deck).
tasks.check: Share of undetermined country reported.

tasks.how: Read the corpus and define 5 specific topics (insight-led names, not generic labels). Quantify each topic with a Boolean keyword set (the full Solr query is generated). Select exact verbatims that illustrate each topic.
tasks.check: Topic overlaps noted. Verbatims copied exactly, with link.
tasks.output: Top topics with volumes and verbatims

tasks.how: List top associated brands and explain each association. List top emojis and what they illustrate. Select max 15 words for the wordcloud (remove the subject's name).
tasks.check: Wordcloud saved in the shared WordArt account, Playfair Display font, brand colours.

tasks.how: Search TikTok with brand + category, product names and format keywords (review, layering, unboxing, mini, dupe, launch) per market. Log every search. Keep 25 to 30 videos published in period N, prioritising views and relevance.
tasks.check: Every retained video is in period N. No duplicates (auto check). Each search is logged.

tasks.how: Fill every column: creator, organic / sponsored, format, product, theme, factual description, exact caption, raw performance numbers.
tasks.check: Numbers entered as raw values (15100000, not '15.1M').

tasks.how: Top hashtags (number of posts, no sponsored hashtags), trending products (cross-check retailer best sellers), associated brands (different from the global ones), main TikTok topics with insight titles, strengths & opportunities. Download GIFs.
tasks.check: Strengths & opportunities differ from global key learnings. Link applied to the full text under each video.

tasks.how: Enter review volumes N and N-1 and average ratings for category, subject and competitors. Run the standard facets (sampled, recommendation, repurchase, brand love).
tasks.tools: Corpus Manager / Live Fix, facet library
tasks.check: Ratings stored as numbers (4.64), not dates.

tasks.how: Use the standard attribute set of the category. Enter category and brand counts. Rank by brand, show category below as the benchmark.
tasks.check: Ranking follows the brand, not the category.

tasks.how: Fill the most reviewed products and select exact verbatims per key attribute.
tasks.check: Product names match the official mapping.

tasks.how: Read growth, market split and peaks. Compare search peaks with social peaks.
tasks.check: Period labels correct on both tables.

tasks.how: Write the 4 key learnings of page 2 (brand perception; volumes, platforms, seasonality, sentiment; top topics; TikTok focus). Answer the brief questions in one line each.
tasks.check: Each KL is backed by a figure or a verbatim. KL differ from TikTok strengths & opportunities.

tasks.how: Transfer figures, verbatims, visuals and footnotes. If an AI assistant was used to rephrase text, reread and tone it down, and tell the reviewer which parts are AI-assisted.
tasks.check: Figures in the deck match this file.

tasks.how: Go through tab 9 and set every line to OK or N/A.
tasks.check: No 'To fix' left.

tasks.how: Send deck + this file to the reviewer on the internal deadline.
tasks.check: Reviewer comments logged.

tasks.how: Remove comments, placeholders, internal shorthand and working notes from the deck. Do not send queries or the production file to the client (queries are internal IP).
tasks.check: No internal notes, no query, no content from another client in the deck.

tasks.how: Integrate comments on the feedback day, run a last check of dates, logos and footnotes, deliver by the client deadline.
tasks.check: Final version named and saved; sources and period in footnotes.

tasks.how: After delivery, update the library: brand profile and launch calendar, product referential, validated query, topic keyword sets, facets, new noise vectors, brand assets. Keep client material within that client's access rights.
tasks.check: Every reusable asset of the digest is saved and dated.

tasks.how: Action client feedback. Log pain points met and the time actually spent per step to refine these timings.
tasks.check: Retro notes saved; actual timings logged.
